root_cause.text: The nexthop replacement path in `net/ipv4/nexthop.c` failed to refresh the `nh_group->has_v4` state when a nexthop changed from AF_INET6 to AF_INET, leaving groups with a stale `has_v4=false` that let `fib6_check_nexthop()` accept IPv6 routes pointing at IPv4-only nexthop members.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says `nh_group_v4_update` was “only called when replacing AF_INET to AF_INET6, but the reverse direction (AF_INET6 to AF_INET) is missed,” and the patch changes `if (oldi->family == AF_INET && newi->family == AF_INET6)` to `if (oldi->family != newi->family)` so the IPv4-indication update runs for any family change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Broaden nexthop group IPv4-indication updates to handle replacements between any differing address families.
intent_record.what: The comment was generalized from describing only an IPv4-to-IPv6 nexthop replacement to describing nexthop replacement between different address families. The condition was changed from `oldi->family == AF_INET && newi->family == AF_INET6` to `oldi->family != newi->family`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the IPv4-indication update logic now runs for any nexthop family change rather than only the specific IPv4-to-IPv6 case. This broadens the path that updates all groups using the nexthop when the address family changes, ensuring the related state stays consistent for both IPv4-to-IPv6 and IPv6-to-IPv4 replacements.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it broadens nexthop group IPv4-state updates when a nexthop is replaced across address families, which would fix the stale nh_group->has_v4 value left after AF_INET6 to AF_INET replacement.

candidates.rationale: This condition only updates IPv4-indication state for AF_INET to AF_INET6 replacements. The root cause is that the reverse replacement path (AF_INET6 to AF_INET) was not handled, so groups could keep a stale has_v4=false.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only refreshed IPv4-indicator state for AF_INET to AF_INET6 replacements. It failed to handle the reverse AF_INET6 to AF_INET case, so nh_group->has_v4 could remain stale false after replacement, which is the root cause of the validation bypass.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the replacement path in `replace_nexthop_single()` and the new fix. The vulnerable construct is exactly the stale IPv4-indication state in nexthop groups after replacement: the commit message says the indication "is not updated when a nexthop is replaced," and the bug scenario is when an IPv4 nexthop is replaced by an IPv6 nexthop. The fix is present here: after `rcu_assign_pointer(old->nh_info, newi);` / `rcu_assign_pointer(new->nh_info, oldi);`, the code checks `if (oldi->family == AF_INET && newi->family == AF_INET6)` and iterates `list_for_each_entry(nhge, &old->grp_list, nh_list)` to call `nh_group_v4_update(nhg);`, which recalculates `nhg->has_v4` from the current members. This directly addresses the stale `has_v4` state, so the vulnerable construct exists in the pre-fix logic, but the shown commit version already contains the fix.
